answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to maintain a long-lived reputation vine: an identity that only gains weight through a history of fulfilled commitments verified by independent counterparties. A new identity that flashes in like a comet and burns out after one transaction earns no trust, while an identity with deep, umber-stained roots — a slow, costly record of honest work — becomes expensive to fake at scale, because each fake must pay the same time and reputation cost as a real one.
